llm.summary: This is a documentation-only HealthKit code review skill, and its sensitive HealthKit examples fit its stated review purpose.

dimensions.detail: The skill does not ask to access local credentials, HealthKit data, networks, user profiles, or broad filesystem content beyond the code being reviewed.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact contains markdown files only, with no executable scripts, dependencies, install hooks, remote fetches, or package metadata requesting runtime authority.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions ask the agent to inspect and cite in-scope HealthKit code paths before making findings; some examples cover sensitive writes and server sync patterns, but they are presented as review examples rather than automatic actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Mentions of Info.plist keys, background delivery, observer queries, and saved query anchors are HealthKit app implementation topics, not persistence mechanisms installed by the skill.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill is scoped to reviewing HealthKit code for authorization, query usage, background delivery, and data type handling; the referenced HealthKit examples support that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this as a HealthKit review aid, not as production code. Treat its write, sleep, characteristic, background-delivery, and server-sync snippets as examples to evaluate carefully, and ensure real apps add explicit user consent, clear privacy disclosure, minimal permissions, and secure handling for any health data access or transmission.
llm.findings:
[RA2] expected: The flagged plist references are HealthKit entitlements and usage-description keys used in reviewed iOS apps; they do not create agent or system persistence.
[SQP-2] expected: The flagged HealthKit read/write and sync snippets involve sensitive health data, but they are documentation examples for code review and are paired with authorization and minimal-permission guidance elsewhere in the skill.
